title: LOTO: Control of Hazardous Energy
body: Maintenance on a stopped machine goes wrong when stored hydraulic pressure, a dead-looking circuit or a re-energised line catches someone inside the work zone. LSR 3 is a defined violation trigger, so a skipped isolation is a personal and reportable failure, not a paperwork slip.
keyPoints: Run all six SWI 21 steps before work starts: identify energy sources, notify affected people, isolate, lock and tag, release stored energy, then verify. Step 6 is the one that gets dropped under schedule pressure. Don't let it go.
Every authorised person puts on their own personal lock and takes the key with them. Nobody removes or shares another person's lock, including on shift change.
Stored energy means hydraulic lines, cylinders, pneumatic receivers and capacitors. Bleed or vent them. A machine that is switched off is not isolated.
apply: Two repair jobs are in the workshop right now, the DT-128 engine swap and the EX-253 slew-gear repair, and hydraulic and stored-energy work on those machines is where a missed verify step is most likely; check the lock register and the verify step on both before anyone goes under the boom or the cab.
